blocks.content: Every open source project exists because someone built something and made it public. You can now contribute to any of them using the workflow you learned.
The hardest part is knowing where to start.
GitHub has a label for this: good first issue.

items: Go to github.com and search for a topic you care about — a language, a framework, a tool you use.
Switch the filter from Repositories to Issues.
Add label:"good first issue" to your search.

blocks.alt: GitHub search results showing issues labeled good first issue

blocks.content: Start small. Fix a typo, update a broken link, or improve an example.
These are real contributions. They become part of a project's history, and they teach you how collaboration works without risk.
👉 Next, let's see what to check before making a change.
Use this space for your doubts about this lesson. Ask us anything that's confusing and our experts will provide explanations to help you understand.
